elements.element: Customer may assign to any affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The affiliate exception is limited to a “financially responsible affiliate,” so it does not permit assignment to every affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: The clause permits either party to assign without approval to a successor in connection with a merger, subject only to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The no-approval successor exception expressly includes an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The no-approval successor exception expressly covers a sale of all or substantially all assets of the assigning party.

elements.element: Vendor may not make any assignment without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without Customer consent to a financially responsible affiliate or to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that either party’s required approval may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no competitor prohibition and could permit assignment to a competitor under an exception or with consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate because of Customer’s change of control.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that no change of control of Client gives TrueLink a right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual successor exception permits Client to assign to a successor without approval in the listed corporate transactions.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor exception is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual successor exception permits TrueLink to assign to a successor without approval in the listed corporate transactions.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor exception is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: A Customer assignment to a financially responsible affiliate requires no consent even when the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The clause states that required approval may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: A Vendor assignment to a financially responsible affiliate requires no consent even when the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The clause states that required approval may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

result.reason: The redline provides mutual successor-assignment rights with written notice, a mutual reasonableness standard, and the requested protection against Vendor termination upon Customer change of control. It does not satisfy the preferred position because Customer’s affiliate right is qualified, Vendor retains no-consent affiliate and successor rights, and there is no competitor prohibition. It does not satisfy the fallback because non-successor affiliate assignments remain exempt from consent. It is not minimal because it reaches neither complete level and additionally expands the change-of-control protection to suspension and repricing and the consent standard to conditioning and delay. The drafting is otherwise coherent and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms, but its operative assignment framework misses material requirements of both positions.
